title: Ephemeral admin elevation via SAML assertions + RBAC v2 audit hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Add support for ephemeral (time-limited) admin elevation that can be granted by SAML assertions or by console-approved workflows while ensuring RBAC v2 rules are enforced and every elevation is recorded in the audit log. Goals:
- Allow IdPs that issue SAML assertions to request temporary admin elevation for a user (e.g., support engineer needs 30m admin access).
- Enforce RBAC v2 policy checks before granting elevation (no bypass of existing allow/deny rules).
- Store a verifiable audit record for each elevation request and grant (including assertions, approver, TTL, origin IP, and revocation events).
- Provide automatic revocation at TTL expiry and a manual revoke API for security operators.
- Surface a compact UI in Org Admin → Activity to show active ephemeral elevations and allow emergency revoke.
Acceptance criteria:
1) Backend API to accept SAML-based elevation requests and console-initiated requests (POST /orgs/:id/elevations).
2) RBAC v2 evaluation path updated to consider ephemeral role overlay and to reject elevations that conflict with org-level deny policies.
3) Audit store entries created for request, approval, grant, and revoke events; entries include assertion raw (hashed), approver id, TTL, and request metadata.
4) TTL-based revocation job that scales across Dedicated clusters and Private instances without central single point of failure.
5) Console UI showing active elevations and a revoke button; feature gated behind admin flag.
6) Integration tests covering SAML assertion parsing, RBAC decision path, audit persistence, and revoke timing.
7) Security review completed and signed-off before rollout.
Implementation notes:
- New data model: Elevation record (id, org_id, user_id, requested_roles, source, assertion_hash, requested_ttl, granted_by, granted_at, expires_at, revoked_by, revoked_at, metadata). Store as first-class rows in primary DB with append-only audit table for compliance retention.
- Use existing audit pipeline (event-shipper -> immutable store) for long-term retention; short-term TTL enforcement should rely on in-memory timers + durable checkpoint to DB for crash recovery.
- SAML: validate signature and map SAML attribute names to requested_roles. Only accept from org-configured IdP endpoints.
- RBAC: evaluate both base roles and ephemeral overlay; ephemeral overlay cannot grant permissions outside the union of user's allowed elevation scope (configurable per org).
- Rate-limit elevation requests per org and per principal to prevent misuse.
- Telemetry: counters for requests, grants, revokes, failed-evaluations; histogram for time-to-grant and time-to-revoke.
Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind `ephemeral_elevations` org-level toggle.
2) Start internal canary (redwood-infra org) for 2 weeks.
3) Open beta for handful of enterprise customers with SAML enabled.
4) Default enable for all orgs after 8 weeks and successful security sign-off.
Migration considerations:
- Backfill: none required. New elevations only.
- Backwards compatibility: existing RBAC checks remain unchanged for users without ephemeral elevations.
Long-term: consider adding OAuth/JIT flow for ephemeral elevation and integration with external approvals (PagerDuty, Slack approvals).
